criteria: From the authenticated public API, Rust-owned Project resource edits and deletion following Project creation return the expected result, preserve response/catalog behavior, and support exact idempotent replay including after restart.

For owned organization resources and Project attachments, the public Node route forwards to signed private Actix/SQLx only for persisted Rust ownership; Node/Drizzle remains the scoped owner-handoff coordinator because Actix exposes no handoff command. Real PostgreSQL races prove the covered in-flight Node writers serialize before owner=fence handoff and stale Node writes fail before business/effect changes; this is scoped fence evidence, not global legacy-writer retirement. Rust outage or unresolved ownership fails closed without a Node fallback or duplicate writer.

Branding preserves legacy validation through the authenticated Rust-owned public path: a well-formed nonexistent logo returns 404, a cross-organization logo returns 422, and both failures leave branding fields/version, receipts, activity, outbox, a pre-existing organization_logos link, and the linked/foreign asset rows unchanged.

SQLx mutation transactions keep business rows, owner/fence state, receipts, activity, and outbox effects consistent; an injected audit failure rolls back, same-key retry commits once, and persisted outbox delivery recovers across restart.

Organization name and description remain editable through their supported Node-owned path while Rust-owned branding fields retain their required-mode authority and exact audit details; unsupported mixed ownership updates are not silently split or double-written.

Existing CLI and MCP organization-branding and Project/Goal contracts remain compatible, including nullable clear semantics, signed actor context, idempotency, and no missing-executable or Node-authority fallback.

Report only real-entry-connected/private verification for this slice; default Rust ingress, global Node writer retirement, implementation_complete, release_ready, and production_verified remain false.

Legacy receipt continuity: an authenticated public generic organization PATCH retry with the same key and exact payload replays an already committed v1-format branding receipt produced by the former generic-route adapter, returns the original branding result, and leaves business state/version/receipt/activity/outbox counts unchanged; a changed payload still conflicts. Since the old v1 receipt has no route-origin marker, an exact-payload legacy receipt produced through the dedicated branding route is indistinguishable; newly written v2 generic receipts remain route-bound.
